# /crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build

lane: cross-cutting | group: Guided walks | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.119.0 | prompts: 7
purpose: Walk a draft spec through architecture, tighten, questions, and the plan until the ready check is clear.
use_when: A spec should be tightened and planned until it is ready to build
prompt_note: The walk's own prompts are the playbook skip or reapply question, asked even when that file is already applied, one batch of optional extras once after open questions when any extra applies, one batch for kept-open questions that still have no Blocks line after the plan, one jump-back card per spec finding during plan review (recommended: run /crav1-tighten-spec on just that finding now; the other option keeps it as an open point and continues; a finding already jumped does not ask again), one same-or-new card when a spec finding is a close reword of a recorded finding (same recorded finding, or this is new), one jump-back question when the ready check is not clear (jump back, or clear a reopened step with nothing new), and the yes before the progress file is written. A reopened tasks-ready-to-build step does not ask that jump-back card. That yes shows the progress line, unless the step's own confirm already included this record. An extra's yes is that case. Questions inside a step belong to that step's skill and its own budget. A value the user left out is outside the budget. A headless run stops before any of these.
reads: Reads the spec folder, the optional playbook, and `walk-progress.md` when resuming. The first command is `scripts/walk_progress.py start --root <folder-or-slug> --vendor copilot`, which returns resume and playbook-status. The ready check is `scripts/walk_progress.py readiness --root <spec-folder> --write-map --vendor copilot`, which reads `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `claims.md` when it exists, and `verify.md` through `task_order.py` and `question_blocks.py`. It fetches the specs repo before it reads. It does not read production data.
writes: Writes `docs/specs/<slug>/walk-progress.md` through `scripts/walk_progress.py --vendor copilot`, and only after a yes that was shown the progress line, unless that step's confirm already included the record. One record per step, right when that step finishes. A spec-finding jump back records `- Jump-back:` with `Continue:`, and a return records `- Open point:`. A close reword records `Alias:` on the first-seen `Key:`. `readiness --write-map` writes `docs/specs/<slug>/build-map.md` in the same format as `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`. The playbook step records `docs/playbooks/<topic>.md`, not the outside path. Spec, plan, and task edits happen inside the skill the walk runs, after that skill's own yes, except a `Blocks:` line (and the matching Risk sentence when it is `Blocks: none` or `Blocks: whole slice`) for a kept-open question that still has no line after the plan. The whole slice writes `- Blocks: whole slice` and the Risk line `kept open; blocks the whole slice until resolved.` A `Blocks:` line wins over that Risk wording. A jump back reruns that skill and does not edit those files, and it does not write `Reviewed:`. `/crav1-resolve-open-questions` with `apply <file>` writes playbook answers and the `docs/playbooks/` copy, including Kept items through the rules of `/crav1-add-to-spec`, and this walk does not call `/crav1-add-to-spec` a second time for those items.
leaves alone: Leaves `spec.md`, `plan.md`, and `tasks.md` to the skills that own them, except that one `Blocks:` pass. Does not change `Answer:` or `Change:` lines in the playbook. Does not start `/crav1-build-tasks`, `/crav1-build-features`, or `/crav1-verify-build-against-spec`. Never writes `verify.md`. Does not git-commit.
limits: A headless run stops. No playbook skips step 1. Architecture review always runs inside the walk even though the new-slice route marks it optional. Needs verify is named and not started. An open plan-review warning is not ready. The progress script does not decide that a playbook was already applied unless this walk recorded that apply.
flow:
- a finding with no topic gets one on the next walk start, derived the same way as a new finding, and `start` returns `topics_line` for that one line.
- leftover wording in plan review is a patch (`--kind stale-wording`), not a full jump back.
- The card header is the name and the code, for example `Static-IP notes (P9)`.
- `clear --step` needs `--card` from that step's reopen card, and a reopen clear is never folded into another step's card.
- A `Stale since` line on or after the latest walk Done date counts as stale seen.
- the Reviewed line uses `plan_check.py open-count --review <file> --vendor copilot` (`open: <n>`).
- Held includes a task that only waits, via `(after:)`, on a task that is not built yet, and the reason is on that held line.
- `clear --yes` fails with `still-reopened` instead of reporting success when nothing cleared.
- The ready check reply is `reply`, which keeps the Source, Build map and Zoom the map lines.
- `readiness` offers `Continue the build walk on <branch>:` only when the walk's claim user (else its `Run yes:` name) matches `--user` or `git config user.name`; someone else's walk is a Waiting line, `T9 to T12 are person B's, built, and wait for PR 82 to merge.` or `T9 to T12 are in progress by person B.` Built claimed tasks read `built by <name>, waits for PR <n> to merge`.
- A reopened step reads one reason sentence, then `Finish the reopened /crav1-tighten-spec step:` above the command.
- A walk's own files never reopen a step.
- when `walk-progress.md` lists a branch run that is not merged and its `build-progress` file is not at `comment`, `wait-merge` or `merge-pr`, Run next starts with `Continue the build walk on <branch>:` above `/crav1-build-walk <slug> <branch>`.
- A behind or diverged specs repo ends with `Merge origin into your local branch, since they have diverged (never rebase):` above `git pull --no-rebase`.
- `--write-map` keeps a done task on its merge commit, not the tick commit.
- `readiness --write-map` keeps each done task on its own commit (from its branch's `build-progress` merge result or its own `verify.md` row), never a commit another task names.
- The open-questions entry is a label line, `Ask the open questions, which haven't been asked yet:`, above `/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions <slug>`, and every Run next entry puts its label above the command, for example `T1 waits until the reopened /crav1-tighten-plan step finishes:` or `T1 and T2 wait until ...`, `Verify the built tasks, since verify.md is behind:`, `Push the specs repo, which is 2 commits ahead of origin:`, `Resolve the open question that blocks the first task:`.
- the record card comes before the ending, so the last reply starts with Run next.
- When only Done or Verify version would change, `record_unchanged` is true and the record is skipped.
- A task waiting on a merge (from `build-progress/<branch>.md`) is waiting, not offered.
- Your own claim reads `T5 is yours; the walk resumes it.`
- the Catch up first line `T# failed verify: <reason>.` is short.
- The reason is the Verify cell's opening sentence, plus the sentence that names the cause (`...
- made the asserts stale.`, `...
- because ...`) when it fits, about 200 characters, cut only at a sentence end; leading run detail (`fail at PR 7's tip abc1234: pipeline 6 run 251, 110 failed, 173 passed.`) gives way to the next sentence.
- The full cell stays in `verify.md`.
- A held question or approval with nobody named says `Nobody is named to answer it yet.` or `Nobody is named to give it yet.`, and the Waiting line says `nobody named for 1`, never `Waiting for not named yet`.
- a fresh verify is never behind.
- An older `Next:` line in `verify.md` is stale only for a ticked task whose own row says Not implemented, claimed done or unverified, or has no row; a Verified or Failed row is current.
- A built task whose verify failed is `T# failed verify: <reason>.` in the Catch up first block, with `Fix T#:` and `/crav1-fix-build-gaps <slug> T#`.
- Needs verify holds only its own task, so ready branches keep their blocks (the result is ready-partial), and questions not asked yet stay a `/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions <slug>` entry after them.
- The Catch up first block never replaces the branch blocks.
- cards follow the card wording rule in `docs/reference/question-cards.md`.
- `spec-finding` prints a `background` sentence and an option `text`, for example `Fix P2 in the spec now, before the plan goes on?`.
- The readiness output adds `reopen_cards`, a plain clear-or-rerun card per reopened step, for example `Skip redoing the plan review?`.
- The record card says what will be saved, without quoting the progress line.
- One own-claimed task reads `Your own claim does not hold it.` `start` and `resume` return `read`, the one reference the next step needs, and the walk opens only that file.
- the plan step writes an `## Approval needed` item when a constraint says a named person gives a yes before something.
- An unapproved item holds only its tasks (`ready-partial`).
- `/crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build` is one guided walk with two starts.
- Without one, step 1 is skipped.
- Locked order: playbook when given; `/crav1-review-architecture` always; `/crav1-tighten-spec` one issue at a time; `/crav1-resolve-open-questions`; `/crav1-plan-from-spec`, which writes `plan.md` and `tasks.md`; `/crav1-review-plan` then `/crav1-tighten-plan`; `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`.
- Research, `/crav1-review-security`, `/crav1-model-data`, `/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions`, and `/crav1-suggest-tests-for-code` are offered only when the spec needs them.
- The progress file is `docs/specs/<slug>/walk-progress.md`.
- An optional extra the walk itself runs is recorded with `- Extra:` when it finishes, and that write does not reopen earlier steps.
- `cover` is optional and only counts a write made outside the walk.
- A hand edit or `/crav1-add-to-spec` between sessions reopens only the steps that change affects.
- After apply, the playbook line is the `docs/playbooks/<topic>.md` path, not the outside path, so resume works on any machine.
- The walk accepts a `docs/playbooks/` path as its playbook argument.
- The walk never reports ready with a blocker, a reopened step, or an open assumption, and it never starts build.
- Before the plan step is recorded, kept-open questions with no `Blocks:` line are offered, one by one or as one batch.
- when the open-questions batch and the progress line share one card, `yes (Recommended)` covers both.
- Typed changes go on that card's free-text answer.
- The optional-extras card is a multi-select and includes None, go to plan.
- the Blocks batch, and the tighten-plan batch inside review-and-tighten-plan, each print a findings table in that same reply before the card.
- The card names each item and its recommendation, for example `P4 tasks miss the 400 path: add a test`.
- It does not say `table above`.
- The card is not asked without the table.
- A cycle, or an after: that names no task, still blocks.
- `readiness --root` builds the rows.
- The walk does not edit spec.md, plan.md, or tasks.md on that jump, and it does not write Reviewed.
- `ack-stamps` acknowledges one shared Done stamp after a yes.
- Next is `/crav1-build-tasks` for the tasks that can start.
- the ready-check ending groups ready tasks and held tasks by the build-map row, the same branch as `scripts/build_map.py --recommend --vendor copilot`.
- A task is `T#` plus its short name.
- each locked step, extra, jump back, and the playbook apply path opens that skill's file from this skill's folder (`../crav1-<name>/SKILL.md`, or the reference that step names, including `references/apply.md` and add-to-spec's fact rules).
- The rule is `docs/reference/open-skill-file.md`.
- `disable-model-invocation: true` stays.
- a spec-tagged finding during plan review is one jump-back card.
- The recommended option runs `/crav1-tighten-spec` on that finding, by opening `../crav1-tighten-spec/SKILL.md`.
- `walk-progress.md` records `- Jump-back:` and, when it comes back, `- Open point:`, each with `Continue:`.
- A plan-tagged finding stays in `/crav1-tighten-plan`.
- The ready check compares `tasks.md` with `verify.md`.
- A ticked task, or a task whose pull request is recorded merged, that `verify.md` still lists as not implemented, or a `Next:` line in `verify.md` that names such a task, makes `verify.md` behind.
- The check prints `Waiting: /crav1-verify-build-against-spec <slug> - verify.md is behind tasks.md (T2, T45)` and does not print that stale Next line.
- The walk never writes `verify.md` and never runs `/crav1-verify-build-against-spec`.
- It still reaches the ready check, which still rewrites `build-map.md` through `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`.
- a `Next:` line is stale only when it names a ticked task.
- A merged `[ ]` row whose only leftover is the tick is not behind.
- A verify-only change does not reopen the ready check and does not force `not-ready`.
- The result stays `ready` or `ready-partial`, and `verify_waiting` is shown when verify is behind.
- Where spec, plan, or tasks drift offers a jump back to the ready check, only the walk's record or `clear --yes` restamps `walk-progress.md`.
- `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build` only writes `build-map.md`.
- The spec folder is `../crav1-tasks-ready-to-build/scripts/resolve_spec.py`.
- `Spec body:` and `Questions version:` split the spec stamp.
- An edit confined to `## Open questions` reopens resolve-open-questions and does not reopen tighten-spec, plan-from-spec, review-and-tighten-plan, or tasks-ready-to-build.
- A question with a `Blocks:` line, or one listed on `Kept questions:`, stays Waiting through that drift.
- A hold inferred from `T#` ids in the question text stays Waiting too.
- A reopened resolve-open-questions step alone does not force `not-ready` when some tasks can start: the result is `ready-partial`, with `resolve_waiting` and a Next line for that step.
- When later steps are reopened, Next is `Next: rerun or clear <steps>.`
- a task checkbox, a `(PR n)` or `(done)` note on that task line, and `(PR n)` or a trailing merged word on a Match `Branch:` line are progress.
- The stamp hashes normalized text and writes `Content stamp: normalized`.
- When `result` is `not-ready` and `can_start` is not empty, that list is not a start.
- Print `because`.
- A progress-only edit leaves a held slice `ready-partial`.
- `scripts/walk_progress.py resolve-stamps --vendor copilot` settles a merge conflict in `walk-progress.md` when every hunk is only a version line.
- `/crav1-finalize-commit` runs it on the pull path.
- `Done` and `Result` stay.
- when the result is `ready`, or `ready-partial` with tasks that can start, each Next line recommends `/crav1-build-walk` with the T number beside the short name and the branch, and names `/crav1-build-tasks` as the alternative for one task without the walk.
- A `not-ready` result does not recommend the walk.
- the spec folder command is `<interpreter> -X utf8 <skill crav1-tasks-ready-to-build>/scripts/resolve_spec.py "<query>" --root docs/specs`.
- On Windows `<interpreter>` is `python` with `PYTHONUTF8=1`.
- Elsewhere it is `python3`.
- Do not run `python3` alone.
- The ready check is `readiness --root <spec-folder>`.
- Playbook status passes `--playbook <file>` as well as `--root`.
- The rule is `docs/reference/running-scripts.md`.
- `walk_progress.py start --root <folder-or-slug> --vendor copilot` resolves a spec folder or a slug the way `resolve_spec.py` does and returns resume and playbook-status in one JSON object.
- A close reword of a recorded spec finding is the same finding: the first-seen `Key:` stays, later wordings are `Alias:`, and the card offers `same recorded finding` or `this is new`.
- An old progress file with only `Key:` still matches those words.
- The ready check is `readiness --root <spec-folder> --write-map`.
- It writes `build-map.md` in the same format as `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build` and the walk does not open that skill.
- `resume` and `readiness` return `reopen_line`.
- A requirement section (Problem, Goals, Non-goals, Users and journeys, Acceptance criteria, Constraints, and the other rows in `references/section-reopen.md`) reopens tighten-spec and the plan steps.
- It does not reopen resolve-open-questions when `changed_questions` is empty.
- The stable key from 1.146.0 ignores a refreshed commit list, and one close reword of a stored question stays that question.
- An explicit `Id:` mark still reopens when the words change.
- `## Match`, `## In the code`, a `Synced at` line, and an already-answered question set `restamp_only` and reopen nothing.
- An older step with no `Section stamps` line still uses the 1.137 rule.
- `readiness` returns `ending`, and that text is the reply.
- On ready and ready-partial, `Run next:` is first, before any Waiting line.
- Each command is alone in a code span and is a complete invocation for a new session: the T#s on that branch, and the slug when `docs/specs` has more than one slice, for example `/crav1-build-walk orders-api T3`.
- Behind or diverged, it stops and Run next is `git pull --no-rebase`.
- A task with an `In progress:` line in `claims.md` is left unchanged, and the walk says once which claimed tasks were kept.
- The ready check holds those tasks as `in progress by <user> since <date>` and does not offer them in Run next.
- A claim older than three days, or `Claim max age:`, warns and is never cleared on its own.
- the ready check's Next lines match Run next, and `M can start now` counts only ready branches.
- `scripts/repo_sync.py --vendor copilot` and `scripts/claims.py` in this skill are thin wrappers to the build-walk copies.
- the walk's references match the 1.153.0 ending: one Run next block at the top, the walk command only there, and no `Next:` line after the Waiting lines.
- A stop prints the walk command in a Run next entry, not a `Next:` line.
- The ending adds one `Loop:` line per pair or ring of branches that wait for each other, and those tasks count as Blocked in the counts and in `build-map.md`.
- Other tasks keep their state, so the result can stay `ready-partial`.
- `walk-progress.md` also holds one `- Branch run:` status line per whole-branch run of `/crav1-build-walk`, under `## Branch runs`.
- Record, cover, and clear keep those lines, `resume` returns them as `branch_runs`, the ready check prints the unmerged ones, and `resolve-stamps` settles a conflict that is only those lines by keeping each branch's newest line.
- the ready check uses the shared walk ending (`scripts/walk_ending.py --vendor copilot`, the same one the standalone ready check and build-walk use), and `readiness` is brief by default; `--full` prints the complete JSON only on an explicit ask.
- the readiness ending follows each `Loop:` line with the fix offer, the recommended fix first (`fix-loop`, then `fix-loop <n>`), and a ready or ready-partial ending adds the Run next entry `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build <slug> fix-loop`.
- The JSON has `loop_card` and `loop_fixes`.
- New subcommand `walk_progress.py fix-loop --root <spec-folder> [--pick <n>] [--yes] --vendor copilot`: without `--yes` it writes nothing and prints the card; with it, it writes `tasks.md` and `build-map.md` and reports what is left.
- the ready-check Loop offer and Run next entry use `fix-loop` and `fix-loop <n>` only.
- The `walk_progress.py fix-loop --vendor copilot` subcommand is unchanged, except a successful preview (no `--yes`) now exits 0.
- A not-ready ending starts with `Run next:` for the first real next step, with a plain reason such as `The plan was reopened for review, so T5, T9 and T43 wait until /crav1-tighten-plan finishes.`
